findings.evidence: Digest dbff837f: "removed units (111, showing 40)". All 40 shown units resolve through valid section rows in sections.json (s001-s022), and the 6 units in digest be9701bf are accepted-drop rows. The other 71 units were not shown, so this judgment could not check them.
findings.fix: Regenerate the dbff837f digest without the cut and confirm that each of the 71 unshown para: units maps through sections.json to a valid row. For any unit that does not map, restore it (into references/ when it is domain-specific, a template users ask for or a tested example; into SKILL.md only when the procedure depends on it) or add a row for it to docs/audit/recovery/commit-work/record.md.

findings.evidence: Step 3 is one paragraph of about ten sentences: the leftover check, mktemp, cleanup on every route, then "Two questions pick the index, then the method" with four nested bullets. Each nested bullet has its own sub-branches (overlap check, temporary index, whole file, part of a file).
findings.fix: Keep every rule but split step 3 into labelled sub-steps: 3a run directory (leftover check, mktemp, cleanup), 3b choose the index (overlap check, temporary index), 3c staging method (whole file, part of a tracked file, untracked file). This keeps the Process pattern scannable at the decision points.

findings.evidence: Step 6 opens with "Take the message vocabulary from the repository, in the order of `references/commit-message-template.md`" and says "the reference's collect-and-ask step applies". It then closes with "Read `references/commit-message-template.md` only when the repository sets its own message rules...", so the trigger for loading the reference is unclear.
findings.fix: Make the opening say the order is inlined and needs no read: "Take the message vocabulary from the repository, in this order: commitlint config, `commit.template`, CONTRIBUTING, a PR template, then recent subjects." Leave the closing gate as the only loading trigger, and state that a conflict between sources is one of its conditions.

findings.evidence: Stage-only branch: "confirm the user's own entries are unchanged: `git ls-files -s -- <their paths>` before and after staging must match". This sits in step 4, which runs after step 3 has already staged, so if you follow the steps in order there is no "before" snapshot.
findings.fix: Move the snapshot into step 3: "Stage-only, before staging anything: record `git ls-files -s -- <the user's staged paths>`." Then have step 4 compare the post-staging output against that record.

findings.evidence: A one-line fix, no body needed: `fix(auth): treat a token at its expiry time as expired`
findings.fix: The three worked messages are templates a user can ask for, so keep them in references/. Move the three lines that only restate Conventional Commits defaults the model already writes (one-line fix needs no body; the body says why; mark a break in the header and the footer) into the Message checklist as one rule, and record that shortening in docs/audit/recovery/commit-work/record.md.

findings.evidence: if `git apply --cached --check` fails, stop and ask, and never edit inside a hunk
findings.fix: Name the failure mode: a failed `--check` means the copied header or a deleted hunk boundary is wrong, and editing a line count or context line makes `git apply` accept a patch that no longer matches the file. Keep the stop-and-ask rule.

findings.evidence: Read `references/split-one-file.md` when one file holds hunks for two different commits
findings.fix: After that sentence add: Do NOT load `references/split-one-file.md` when the file is wholly approved, the hunks belong to one commit, or the file is untracked (ask for the approved content instead).

findings.evidence: The summary starts with a concrete verb (`fix`, `add`, `remove`, `rename`) rather than `Update` or `Change`.
findings.fix: Add the condition: this applies only when the repository has no subject-case rule. Under `@commitlint/config-conventional`, `subject-case` rejects a capitalised verb, so the summary stays lowercase (`fix(auth): treat a token at its expiry time as expired`).

findings.evidence: Shows ordered `git status`, `git diff`, `git add -- src/auth.ts`, `git diff --cached`, and `git commit` commands.
findings.fix: review-and-commit omits the scratch directory the workflow always creates. Assert a proposed `mktemp -d "$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/commit-work.XXXXXX"` and an `rm -rf -- "<run>"` of only that directory, and keep the existing ordered status, diff, add, cached-diff and commit assertions.

findings.evidence: When the user approved a path's staged diff, commit that exact staged version and never restage the whole working-tree file over it
findings.fix: Before the overlap check, add the case the approved path also has unstaged edits: `git add -- <path>` would replace the approved staged blob. Copy the staged blob with `git diff --cached --binary -- <path>` and `git apply --cached` into the temporary index (or leave it untouched in the real index) and do not `git add` that path.

findings.evidence: previous-version digest: meme-factory at dbff837f: 'removed units (463, showing 40)'. All 40 items shown are explained by rows in record.md or sections.json, but the other 423 units could not be checked.
findings.fix: Rerun the removal check with the full digest (no cut list) so every removed unit since dbff837f can be matched to a record row or a destination. Add a row in docs/audit/recovery/meme-factory/record.md for any unit that has none.

findings.evidence: Step 1: 'Before answering, apply step 4's audience questions (who will see it, who is the butt of the joke, the channel's tone)'. Step 4 then lists the same three questions in full: 'Who will see it: team Slack, a PR, or a public post? Who is the butt of the joke...'
findings.fix: In step 1, keep only the pointer 'apply step 4's audience questions' and drop the repeated parenthetical. The full questions stay in step 4, so nothing is lost.

findings.evidence: The text-only branch (step 1) only sends the agent to other files and then says 'answer in text and stop'. The image branch has a full procedure (redact, pick template, write joke, build, check), but the text branch has no matching check in SKILL.md, for example confirming the format fits its container.
findings.fix: Add one line to step 1: 'Then check the result against the format's Needs line and container in references/text-memes.md (fence for greentext, ASCII and chat logs; nested blockquotes for chains) before answering.'

findings.evidence: Several evals set "files": ["references/markdown-memes-guide.md"] (and image-memes.md, blog-posts.md, text-memes.md). Those are the skill's own reference files, not user input files under evals/files/. Also, `generate` has no structured (--json) output, while `suggest` and `list-templates` do.
findings.fix: Move the reference names to a separate field such as "expected_reads" and keep "files" for real inputs under evals/files/ (none are needed today). Optionally add --json output to `generate` (for example {"url":...,"markdown":...}) and a test for it in tests/skills/meme-factory/test_meme_generator.py.

findings.evidence: generate_parser.add_argument("--alt", default="Meme", ...). If the agent passes --markdown without --alt, the output is ![Meme](...), which breaks SKILL.md step 6: 'Present the result as a Markdown image whose alt text describes both the picture and the joke.' get_markdown_image also does not escape ']' in alt text.
findings.fix: When --markdown is set without --alt, exit with an error ('--alt is required with --markdown: describe the picture and the joke'). Escape ']' in the alt text inside get_markdown_image. Add tests for both cases in tests/skills/meme-factory/test_meme_generator.py.

findings.evidence: removed units (463, showing 40)
findings.fix: The cut list is recorded in docs/audit/recovery/meme-factory/record.md; keep the record, do not restore the 463 units in bulk.

findings.evidence: Step 1 routes text-only, step 5 routes the helper, and image details sit in references/image-memes.md, but SKILL.md still carries the full escape table, query-parameter list and worked URLs instead of staying a short router.
findings.fix: Keep the workflow, template table and gotchas in SKILL.md; move the escape table and worked URLs into references/image-memes.md and load them only when building a URL by hand.

findings.evidence: The watermark gotcha says the public API has no watermark parameter because OpenAPI lists none, but does not say what a caller who wants the mark gone should do instead.
findings.fix: Add one line: the public renderer always draws its own mark, so tell the user it cannot be removed through the URL rather than inventing a parameter.

findings.evidence: Step 1 says to read references/markdown-memes-guide.md for every text-only request, then also read references/text-memes.md for one of the 15 named formats, even though the guide is only a pointer into text-memes.md.
findings.fix: Load references/text-memes.md for a named text format and references/markdown-memes-guide.md only for the greentext, copypasta and ASCII fence rules; say not to load both unless both are needed.

findings.evidence: `color` is documented as `<name or hex>[,<name or hex>]` with examples `red,blue` or `FF80ED`, and `center` and `scale` are named with no default or worked value, while the helper cannot emit any of the three.
findings.fix: Give one default (`color` omitted, or `FFFFFF,000000`) and one hand-built example for `center` and `scale`, and say to omit all three unless the user asked for them.

findings.evidence: The 14 eval prompts have verifiable assertions, but no evals/files/ inputs, and trigger-queries.json has 12 should-trigger and 10 should-not-trigger queries with no train/validation split.
findings.fix: Add one eval input file under evals/files/ for the sensitive-caption case, and split trigger-queries.json into a fixed train set and a validation set with both polarities in each.

findings.evidence: Step 5 says never call generate with a caption count different from the template's lines, but the helper accepts any number of captions and the skill gives no check before the call.
findings.fix: Before calling generate, compare the caption count with the template's lines (table, list-templates, or /templates/<id>) and stop to ask when they differ.

findings.evidence: The emojicore sample is four lines of replacement characters (`���� leaving my responsibilities`) instead of the emoji the tips tell the agent to use as syntax.
findings.fix: Replace those four lines with the original emoji (or name the emoji in words) so the sample can be adapted.

All 40 shown items and the deleted skill-rules-fragment.json are explained by record.md rows: each section row is valid through the sections.json units, and the accepted-drop rows stand.
findings.fix: Regenerate the dbff837f digest without truncation and check the 82 unshown units against docs/audit/recovery/mui/record.md. findings.evidence: "**Icon-only buttons.** An `IconButton` has no accessible name of its own: set `aria-label` to the action"
findings.fix: This is general a11y knowledge the model mostly has (activation, not expert). Keep it, but shorten it to one clause, or tie it to a MUI-specific trap such as Tooltip title not naming the button, so it earns its line.

findings.evidence: "4. **Apply the matching trap** from v7 facts and Gotchas."
findings.fix: Make step 4 a short thinking prompt instead of a pointer. For example: "Before editing each hit, ask: is this a slot rename, a Grid prop, a theme build or a styling-specificity problem? Then apply the matching v7 fact and the Gotcha that names its silent failure."

findings.evidence: "Palette augmentation, `colorSchemes`, CSS layers and nested themes are in `theme-customization.md`; beating a state class is in `styling-guide.md`." Both files live in `resources/`. The bare names resolve neither from `references/` nor from the skill root.
findings.fix: Use skill-root-relative paths: `resources/theme-customization.md` and `resources/styling-guide.md`. Do the same for the `styling-guide.md` mention in the TextField bullet.

findings.evidence: "state-class specificity and color-mode styling are in `styling-guide.md`; theme-level defaults are in `theme-recipes.md`". `styling-guide.md` is in `resources/`, so the bare name does not resolve. The last paragraph repeats "(`styling-guide.md`)".
findings.fix: Write `resources/styling-guide.md` and `references/theme-recipes.md` (skill-root-relative), as the spec's file-reference rule requires.

findings.evidence: Input paths are inconsistent: "files": ["legacy-api.tsx"]. Recipe evals list skill files as inputs: "files": ["references/component-recipes.md"]. Several prompts are terse one-liners ("MUI v7 confirmation dialog for deleting project, with cancel/delete.").
findings.fix: Point every input at `evals/files/<name>.tsx`. Drop the skill's own reference files from `files`, because the skill loads them itself. Add realistic context (file paths, the repo's typecheck script) to at least two of the terse prompts.

findings.evidence: The step 3 sweep searches "`components=`, `componentsProps=`, `onBackdropClick`, `<Grid item`, deep `@mui/material/<Component>/` imports and `inputProps=` (TextField)". The v7 facts slot list also renames `InputProps`, `InputLabelProps`, `PaperProps` and `TransitionComponent`, and removes `Hidden`, but the sweep never searches for them, so those hits are missed in a full migration.
findings.fix: Extend the sweep list to: `components=`, `componentsProps=`, `onBackdropClick`, `<Grid item`, `<Hidden`, deep `@mui/material/<Component>/` imports, `inputProps=`, `InputProps=`, `InputLabelProps=`, `PaperProps=` and `TransitionComponent=`.

findings.evidence: The first 30 lines restate what a model already knows: MUI is popular, use theme tokens, type sx, build responsively, and a trigger-phrase list the description already carries.
findings.fix: Move the user-facing overview (Purpose through Trigger phrases) into a short README lead, and record the generic remainder (How It Works steps 1 and 3-5, Theme Integration, Responsive Design) in docs/audit/recovery/mui/record.md; keep the v7-specific bullets.

findings.evidence: 35 queries, 19 should-trigger and 16 should-not, but 11 of the 16 negatives share no MUI keyword (plain CSS, Chakra, Vue, Vite, Tailwind) and several positives are restatements of the description.
findings.fix: Replace the obvious negatives with near-misses that name Material UI but need a neighbour the description excludes (MUI X date picker, Joy UI, Base UI, a native dialog beside an MUI screen) and add casual should-trigger queries that never say v7, sx or slots.

findings.evidence: The MuiButton example puts `variants` inside `styleOverrides.root` while also setting `borderRadius: 8` on that same slot object, so the slot style is an object that contains a variants array rather than CSS.
findings.fix: Split the slot: keep CSS properties on `styleOverrides.root` and put the `variants` array where the cited v9 'Button CSS classes' section places it, or show both forms and say which one the installed 7.3 and 9.5 theme types accept.
